pairs.subject: multi-speaker-speech-production
pairs.evidence: tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/text.py:4 The sidecar is the live runtime speak path: one character voice (one --sid per process), with sentences split to get the first audio out fast. The golden path says this kind of path belongs to the voice-I/O subject, not to offline multi-speaker script production. Searching tools/voice for stale, render_key, consent, seam, scene, continuity and pronunciation found no hits. The only 'lexicon' is Kokoro's stock lexicon-us-en.txt file, not a per-world dictionary.

techniques.evidence: tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/text.py:4 Lines are split for latency (first audio early), not because a script is longer than the engine's cap. The technique's 'When not to use it' section says latency chunking of a reply is a runtime concern owned elsewhere.

tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/sidecar.py:7 Each say is a live line: it is rendered, streamed and forgotten. There is no stored script, no render record and no reviewed clip to protect from regeneration.

tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/__main__.py:57 One voice per process, chosen at launch from the operator's local Kokoro voices file (stock or blended). There is no cast of cloned voices to carry across vendor engine generations.

tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/plus.py:2 Direction comes in as a separate structured parameter {emotion, intensity, pace} and is mapped to speed, blend, pause and pitch levers. Nothing is inline in the text. The technique's 'When not to use it' section excludes engines that take direction as a separate parameter.

tools/voice/shadowrunr_voice/engine.py:154 The only lexicon is the engine's stock US-English file, passed through when it exists. There is no versioned per-world lexicon, and no script revision whose blast radius would need computing.
